messages:
maya: heads up — svc-x alerted but incidentbot did not page the oncall between 09:02-09:12. customers reported delayed responses.
ops-oncall: confirmed, I didn't get a page. saw an internal webhook error in the incident log at ~09:03.
sre-bot: automated note: circuit-breaker:svc-x triggered cooldown for webhook-forwarder (threshold=5/min). reason: downstream 503 spikes.
alex: I rolled a config tweak to the breaker at 09:00 (reduce sensitivity) — might be related. putting a tag on the deploy.
ryan: @alex what exactly changed? can we revert fast if this is blocking pages?
alex: changed `breaker.window_ms` from 2000 -> 500, and `cooldown_secs` from 30 -> 300 to reduce thrash. intended to stop a noisy upstream.
jamie: oh, that cooldown sounds like it would suppress retries for a long time. could be why incidentbot gave up.
sre-bot: dump of last events (abridged):
```
09:01:58 webhook-forwarder POST /svc-x -> 503 (x6)
09:02:05 breaker tripped (consecutive 5) -> enter cooldown for 300s
09:02:07 incidentbot: page attempt queued -> suppressed (breaker_cooldown)
```
ops-oncall: so incidentbot queued the page but the forwarder suppressed it — we have a blind spot. any manual workarounds?
alex: immediate mitigation: reverting `cooldown_secs` to 30 and restarting forwarder. I'm pushing a rollback now (canary first).
ryan: while that rolls: can someone manually page the oncall for svc-x and check pager delivery for customers impacted? @jamie can you run manual pages + confirm SMS fallback?
jamie: manual pages sent to oncall at 09:07, sms fallback checked — SMS provider accepting messages, but incidentbot's suppression prevented automated escalation.
pagerbot: system: manual page delivered to oncall @ops-team (SMS + push). ack pending.
ops-oncall: acked at 09:09. starting triage with SRE. customer-ops, please notify affected customers with ETA.
customer-ops: emailing two impacted customers now. note: CustomerA reported 6-minute delay in ticket creation; CustomerB flagged elevated latency.
alex: rollback canary finished at 09:10; full rollback started 09:11. monitoring forwarder health.
sre-bot: forwarder healthy: success rate > 99% after 09:12. incidentbot resumed normal paging at 09:12:10.
maya: thanks team. let's capture timeline and assign postmortem owner.
ryan: I'll own the postmortem. action items: (1) revert dangerous cooldown defaults from config (PR), (2) add a safety that if incidentbot queues but forwarder is in cooldown for >10s we escalate via alternate path, (3) add unit test for breaker->suppressor interaction.
jamie: + add runbook step to manually page if automated page suppressed (quick grep command included).
ops-oncall: adding entries to oncall runbook now.
maya: customer impact summary to include in postmortem: two customers affected, delayed pages ~6-10m, no lost pages after manual intervention.
ryan: assigning timeline owner and opening PM for the postmortem doc. estimated RTB (root cause & fix) PR by EOD.
alex: apologies — my change had unintended coupling with incidentbot. will be more conservative in future and run local integration test.
maya: followup: tag `incident-tooling` and schedule a 30m retrofit to harden forwarder fallback. :eyes:
jamie: note: added metric alert for forwarder-suppression-rate > 1/min to avoid silent windows.
ops-oncall: closing live mitigation — handoff to postmortem. good job everyone. :thumbsup:
